steps.intent: Russia's primary objective is to mandate a genuine, professional, on-site investigation by the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission in Douma and establish a credible successor to the discredited JIM (the United Nations Independent Mechanism of Investigation) that respects Syrian sovereignty and guards against politically motivated allegations used as a pretext for Western military strikes. We expect intense opposition from the Western permanent members regarding the strict requirement for on-site verification with verified chain-of-custody, equitable geographic representation in staff recruitment, and the provision reserving the ultimate determination of attribution and punitive measures exclusively to the Security Council.

Côte d’Ivoire.change: Directs that UNIMI and the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission shall carry out their work in full independence, utilizing established international verification standards and all relevant and verifiable sources of information, including on-site visits where feasible, rigorous chain-of-custody protocols for environmental and biomedical samples, and direct witness testimony;

delete paragraph or replace with: 'Requests that UNIMI report its findings directly to the Security Council and the OPCW Executive Council to facilitate appropriate action in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations;'

Ethiopia.change: Directs that UNIMI and the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission shall conduct their work in accordance with established international verification standards and highest professional protocols, utilizing all credible, verifiable, and direct evidence collected through on-site visits, chain-of-custody procedures, and witness interviews;

Underscores that the Security Council, acting in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations, shall consider the findings and conclusions of UNIMI with a view to determining appropriate measures against those identified as responsible for the use of chemical weapons;

France.change: Delete paragraph 9 entirely to ensure that the findings and technical assessments of the mechanism are fully independent and not subject to political vetting or veto by the Security Council.

Delete paragraph 4, or replace it with language affirming that the mechanism shall have full independence to determine its investigative methodology and assess all credible sources of evidence in line with established OPCW standards.

Delete 'for the Council's review and approval' so that the Secretary-General and OPCW Director-General may independently establish the terms of reference without further procedural blocking in the Council.
Delete the reference welcoming the readiness of the Syrian authorities to provide facilitation and security guarantees.

Kuwait.change: Replace with: 'Underscores that UNIMI shall independently submit its findings and conclusions to the Security Council, and reaffirms the prerogative of the Security Council to consider appropriate measures against those identified as responsible for the use of chemical weapons, acting in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations;'

Replace with: 'Directs that UNIMI and the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission shall carry out their work independently, impartially, and thoroughly, utilizing all credible and relevant sources of information and evidence in accordance with established international standards and verification procedures;'
Delete 'for the Council's review and approval' and replace with 'for the information of the Security Council;'

Netherlands.change: Delete paragraph 9 entirely, or replace with text reaffirming the full independence and impartiality of the mechanism's findings and conclusions without subjecting them to a political filter or review by the Security Council.

Delete paragraph 4 or replace it with language that does not restrict the investigative methodologies of the OPCW and UN, ensuring investigators have full discretion to use all credible sources and established forensic standards without arbitrary limitations.
Delete 'for the Council's review and approval' to prevent a political veto over the mechanism's terms of reference and practical modalities.

Peru.change: Delete the restriction 'rather than unverified open-source materials or information provided by partisan entities' and ensure the mechanism and the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission retain full operational autonomy to use all reliable sources and established investigative methodologies.

Replace 'for the Council's review and approval' with 'for the Council's information', ensuring the Secretary-General and the OPCW can operationalize the mechanism without subject to procedural or political deadlock.

Delete 'The final assessment of the findings of UNIMI, as well as' so that the mechanism's technical findings are fully independent and not subject to political approval or veto in the Security Council.

Poland.change: Delete 'rather than unverified open-source materials or information provided by partisan entities' and ensure that the mechanism has full discretion to collect, evaluate, and utilize all relevant and credible sources of information and evidence in accordance with established international investigative standards.
Delete 'for the Council's review and approval' to prevent the operational launch and mandate terms of the mechanism from being subject to political blockage or veto.

Delete paragraph 9 entirely, as any investigative mechanism must be genuinely independent and its professional findings and attribution of responsibility must not be subordinated to political filtering or veto in the Security Council.

Sweden.change: Delete paragraph 4 entirely, or amend to affirm that UNIMI and the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission shall conduct their investigations and determine their methodology in full operational independence, without political interference or preconceived restrictions on sources of information.
Replace 'for the Council's review and approval' with 'for the information of the Security Council'

United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort.change: Delete paragraph 9 in its entirety to ensure that the mechanism's investigative findings are genuinely independent and not subject to political review, filtering, or veto by the Security Council.

Delete paragraph 4 or amend it to remove prescriptive constraints on the collection of evidence, ensuring the mechanism retains full operational independence to utilize all established OPCW investigative methodologies, forensic tools, and credible information sources.
Delete 'for the Council's review and approval' to prevent the operational launch and terms of reference of the mechanism from being subjected to political deadlock and vetoes.

United States of America.change: Delete paragraph 4 in its entirety, or replace with text reaffirming the full operational independence of investigators to collect, evaluate, and assess all available and credible sources of information without political interference or artificial constraints.
Delete 'for the Council's review and approval' to ensure that the establishment of any investigative mechanism cannot be subjected to a subsequent veto or political paralysis.
Specify that the mechanism is established under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations and modeled on the independent mandate of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia expresses its full support for the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation. We firmly believe that any allegations regarding the use of chemical weapons must be thoroughly, objectively, and impartially investigated without politicization or predetermined conclusions. Establishing an independent mechanism based on direct, verifiable on-site evidence and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic is the only credible path forward.
messages.China: China appreciates the Russian Federation's initiative and supports the draft resolution to establish an independent, objective, and impartial investigation mechanism. We have consistently opposed the use of chemical weapons by any party under any circumstances and maintain that investigations must be depoliticized, strictly adhere to rigorous evidentiary standards, and respect Syria's sovereignty. We urge all Council members to engage constructively and work towards consensus on this important matter.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire firmly condemns the use of chemical weapons under any circumstances and supports the establishment of a credible, professional, and impartial investigative mechanism. For this mechanism to command international confidence, it must possess genuine operational independence in gathering evidence and presenting its technical findings without political preconditions. We urge the penholder to engage in constructive dialogue with all Council members to bridge existing divisions and achieve a consensual text.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea reiterates its principled and unequivocal condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by any party, anywhere, and under any circumstances. We support the prompt establishment of an impartial, transparent, and depoliticized mechanism to investigate the grave allegations in Douma and ensure accountability. We encourage the penholder to continue engaging with all Council members to foster consensus and preserve Council unity on this critical issue.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia reiterates its principled and unequivocal condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, and under any circumstances, and stresses the urgent need for a credible, professional, and independent mechanism to establish accountability. We support the initiative to establish such an investigative mechanism and welcome the deployment of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission to Douma. To secure the broadest possible Council unity and avoid division on such a vital matter, we encourage the penholder to show flexibility in accommodating the concerns of other delegations regarding investigative autonomy and methodology.
messages.France: France cannot accept a draft that fundamentally undermines the independence of international chemical weapons investigations and subordinates the determination of responsibility to a political filter and Council veto. Following the horrific chemical attack in Douma, the international community requires a truly independent, impartial, and robust attribution mechanism, not a hollow instrument designed to shield perpetrators. Unless the proposed mechanism is granted genuine operational autonomy free from political interference, France will vote against this text.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan firmly condemns the use of chemical weapons by any party under any circumstances and considers the establishment of an objective, impartial, and professional investigative mechanism to be of utmost necessity. We welcome the deployment of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission to Douma and support the creation of UNIMI as a constructive step toward filling the accountability gap left after the expiration of the Joint Investigative Mechanism. We urge all Council members to demonstrate flexibility and work constructively to bridge existing divisions and adopt a unified approach.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait reiterates its principled and categorical condemnation of the use of chemical weapons anywhere, by anyone, and under any circumstances, and stresses the urgent need for a credible, independent, and impartial mechanism to identify perpetrators and ensure accountability. To ensure the credibility and effectiveness of the proposed mechanism, it is essential that its operational independence and technical findings are fully safeguarded from political interference or veto. We urge the penholder to take these concerns into account in order to foster Council unity and establish an effective accountability mechanism.
messages.Netherlands: The Kingdom of the Netherlands cannot support this draft in its current form, as it fundamentally compromises the independence, professional integrity, and credibility of any future attribution mechanism. An effective mechanism must be genuinely independent and free from political interference, rather than allowing the Security Council to cherry-pick or veto its factual findings. We urge the penholder to align the text with the established standards of the Joint Investigative Mechanism and support genuine, depoliticized accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria.
messages.Peru: Peru is committed to combating impunity and unequivocally condemns the use of chemical weapons, including the horrific reports from Douma. While we support the establishment of an impartial mechanism to identify perpetrators, such a mechanism must be strictly independent, credible, and free from political interference or Council vetoes over its technical findings. We urge the penholder to amend provisions that undermine the operational independence and standard methodologies of the OPCW and the proposed mechanism.
messages.Poland: Poland stands firmly against impunity for the abhorrent use of chemical weapons in Syria and underscores the imperative of establishing a truly independent, professional, and depoliticized attribution mechanism. The current draft fundamentally undermines the independence of the proposed mechanism by granting the Security Council political oversight over its findings and by placing undue restrictions on the methodology and evidentiary standards of the investigators. Unless these provisions are removed to guarantee a credible and unhindered investigation, Poland cannot support this text.
messages.Sweden: Sweden is steadfast in its commitment to accountability for the horrific use of chemical weapons in Syria and supports establishing an effective, professional, and genuinely independent attribution mechanism. However, we cannot support a mechanism whose investigative methods are micromanaged or whose findings are subject to political filtering and a Security Council veto, as currently stipulated in operative paragraphs 4 and 9. If this mechanism is to have any credibility, it must enjoy full operational autonomy and integrity free from political control.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot accept a mechanism that is designed to be crippled from inception. This draft subordinates independent expert attribution to political control, allowing the Security Council—and those with a veto—to pick and choose findings and block accountability for the horrific atrocities seen in Douma. A credible mechanism must be truly impartial, independent, and empowered to identify perpetrators without political interference.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this draft text, which creates a sham investigative mechanism designed to shield the Assad regime and subvert genuine accountability. Operative paragraphs 4, 7, and 9 strip the proposed mechanism of any real independence by micromanaging its methodologies and granting the Security Council—and therefore Russia—a veto over its terms of reference and its ultimate findings. If the Council is to establish a credible mechanism to identify perpetrators of chemical weapons attacks in Syria, it must be truly independent, professional, and free from political manipulation.

steps.summary: The Russian delegation has submitted a constructively revised draft resolution that bridges divisions across the Council while safeguarding the integrity of chemical weapons investigations. Substantial modifications were made to OP4, OP7, and OP9 to ensure the mechanism's professional independence, remove perceived political filters on factual findings, and align procedures with established UN Charter prerogatives, while maintaining indispensable requirements for rigorous chain-of-custody, on-site verification, and respect for Syrian sovereignty.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia fully supports the draft resolution as presented. It is essential that any investigation into the alleged use of chemical weapons be conducted in a strictly objective, transparent, impartial, and depoliticized manner, respecting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We commend the emphasis on direct on-site visits and established chain-of-custody protocols, and we reject any attempt to use unverified allegations as a pretext for unilateral military action.
messages.China: China supports the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. We have consistently opposed the use of chemical weapons by any party, anywhere, and support a comprehensive, objective, and impartial investigation based on verifiable facts and established procedures. We appreciate the draft's emphasis on respecting the sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic, upholding strict chain-of-custody protocols, and preserving the authority of the Security Council.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire reiterates the urgent necessity of establishing an impartial, independent, and professional investigative mechanism to identify those responsible for the heinous use of chemical weapons in Syria. While we welcome the penholder's efforts to incorporate elements of independence, the draft must not constrain investigators' operational methodology or circumvent reporting to the OPCW Executive Council. We urge the penholder to bridge remaining divides with Council members to achieve the consensus essential for a credible, effective mechanism.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the draft resolution and all constructive efforts to establish an impartial, independent, and professional mechanism to investigate allegations of chemical weapons use in Syria, including in Douma. We reiterate our categorical condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, and under any circumstances, and emphasize that those responsible must be held accountable. We urge all Council members to bridge their differences and work towards consensus to ensure that truth and justice prevail.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia appreciates the penholder's constructive accommodation of our proposals in the revised draft, particularly regarding evidentiary standards and the role of the Council under the Charter. We reiterate our firm stance that the use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, is unacceptable and warrants an independent, impartial, and highly professional investigative mechanism to ensure accountability. As our concerns have been addressed, we are ready to support the draft resolution as it stands and urge all Council members to work towards unity on this critical issue.
messages.France: France cannot accept a text that undermines the independence of international chemical weapons investigations by imposing prescriptive methodologies and subjecting technical findings to Council veto. Any attribution mechanism must be truly impartial, credible, and free from political interference, in line with the established standards of the Joint Investigative Mechanism. Unless these core structural flaws are fully addressed, France will vote against this draft.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan fully supports the prompt deployment of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission to Douma and the establishment of a professional, impartial, and depoliticized investigative mechanism to identify perpetrators. We urge all Council members to bridge differences and demonstrate unity in ensuring accountability for any use of chemical weapons, which is unacceptable under any circumstances. We stand ready to support this draft resolution as presented.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait appreciates the penholder's efforts to reflect our views regarding the independent reporting of the mechanism in OP9. Nevertheless, to ensure the mechanism is truly credible, effective, and free from politicization or operational constraints, it is vital that its methodology remains autonomous and that the launch of its work is not delayed by procedural hurdles in the Council. We strongly encourage the penholder to adopt these remaining modifications so that the Council can achieve the broadest possible consensus on accountability for chemical weapons use.
messages.Netherlands: The Kingdom of the Netherlands cannot accept a mechanism whose independence, autonomy, and established methodologies are compromised from the outset. Mandating rigid operational criteria such as indispensable on-site visits allows perpetrators to obstruct investigations simply by denying access or tampering with crime scenes. We insist on a truly impartial, independent, and professional attribution mechanism capable of ensuring full accountability for the horrific attack in Douma and all chemical weapons use in Syria.
messages.Peru: Peru appreciates the adjustments made by the penholder, particularly regarding the independent submission of findings. However, to guarantee an effective, depoliticized, and genuinely independent accountability mechanism that leaves no room for impunity, it is essential that the terms of reference in OP7 do not require Council approval or consideration that could paralyze its deployment. Full technical autonomy and alignment with established OPCW standards must be unequivocally preserved.
messages.Poland: Poland remains deeply committed to establishing a truly independent, impartial, and professional mechanism to identify perpetrators of chemical weapons attacks in Syria. Regrettably, the revised draft still fails to provide the necessary safeguards to protect the mechanism's operational independence and integrity from political interference. Unless the Council can agree on a mechanism that guarantees genuine accountability without political preconditions or vetoes, Poland cannot support this text.
messages.Sweden: Sweden remains firmly committed to ensuring accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria through a truly independent, impartial, and highly professional mechanism. However, this text continues to compromise the operational independence of the proposed mechanism by micromanaging its investigative methodology and subjecting its work and findings to political filtering in the Security Council. Unless the mechanism is granted genuine autonomy without Council interference, Sweden cannot support this draft.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support this draft in its current form as it seeks to replace the Joint Investigative Mechanism with a flawed body subject to political control and veto. Despite minor drafting adjustments, the text continues to micro-manage investigative methodologies and leaves the mechanism's operational mandate and conclusions vulnerable to Council interference. If the Council is to establish a credible mechanism to identify perpetrators of chemical attacks in Syria, it must be genuinely independent, impartial, and free from political vetoes designed to shield the Syrian regime.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot accept a mechanism designed to shield the Syrian regime and subject professional investigations to political control and veto. Any credible accountability mechanism must be established under Chapter VII, enjoy full operational and evidentiary independence, and take effect without procedural bottlenecks. Unless these fundamental deficiencies are addressed, the United States will vote against this draft.

reasons.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia supports an impartial, depoliticized investigation that respects Syrian sovereignty and the UN Charter, aligning with its consistent policy of opposing unilateral Western military intervention and supporting Russian-led multilateral initiatives on chemical weapons in Syria.
reasons.China: China consistently supports an objective, impartial, and professional investigation into alleged chemical weapons use in Syria based on established international standards and respect for state sovereignty, and previously supported Russian and Bolivian initiatives to establish or reform investigative mechanisms; therefore, China votes in favour of the Russian draft resolution.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: While Côte d’Ivoire supports the establishment of an independent, impartial mechanism to investigate allegations of chemical weapons use and hold perpetrators accountable, the draft resolution lacks consensus among Council members, particularly the permanent members, and does not fully address key concerns regarding the mechanism's independence and evidentiary standards. Consistent with Côte d’Ivoire's policy of promoting unity and constructive multilateralism, Côte d’Ivoire abstains.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea consistently supports impartial and objective multilateral mechanisms to investigate alleged chemical weapons use in Syria, and aligns with efforts to preserve unity and consensus in accordance with its indicated support during consultations.
reasons.Ethiopia: Ethiopia consistently supports establishing an independent, impartial, and professional mechanism to investigate chemical weapons allegations in Syria, and aligns with its established position during negotiations in favour of the draft resolution.
reasons.France: The Russian draft resolution undermines the independence and integrity of any attribution mechanism by subjecting investigative findings to Security Council political oversight and imposing restrictive methodologies, directly crossing France's red lines. In line with France's firm policy against impunity for chemical weapons use in Syria and its alliance with the US and UK, France must vote against.
reasons.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan consistently supports impartial, professional, and depoliticized investigations into alleged chemical weapons use in Syria, and aligns with efforts establishing an independent investigative mechanism as proposed in the draft.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait consistently supports genuine accountability for the use of chemical weapons in Syria and favors an independent, impartial mechanism without political interference or Security Council veto over findings; because the draft resolution maintains provisions that compromise the mechanism's complete independence, Kuwait abstains.
reasons.Netherlands: The Russian draft resolution compromises the independence and operational integrity of any chemical weapons attribution mechanism by imposing restrictive evidentiary conditions and subjecting findings to political interference. Because our red-line amendments were rejected and the text does not guarantee an impartial, independent investigation, the Netherlands votes against.
reasons.Peru: Peru cannot support the draft resolution because our red-line amendment to operational paragraph 7 was rejected, leaving the establishment and operationalization of the mechanism subject to Security Council review and political vetoes, thereby compromising its independence and effectiveness.
reasons.Poland: The Russian draft resolution compromises the genuine independence and impartiality of the proposed investigative mechanism by giving the Security Council a political veto over its findings and establishing restrictive methodological conditions that undermine effective accountability for chemical weapons use. Because our essential amendments were completely rejected, Poland votes against the text in solidarity with our European and transatlantic partners.
reasons.Russian Federation: As the penholder and sponsor of this draft resolution proposing the creation of the United Nations Independent Mechanism of Investigation (UNIMI), Russia votes firmly in favour to advance an objective, strictly regulated investigation that respects Syria's sovereignty and Security Council prerogatives.
reasons.Sweden: Sweden cannot support a mechanism whose independence and operational integrity are compromised by prescriptive investigative methodologies and provisions that subject the investigators' findings and terms of reference to political filtering and approval by the Security Council. As our red lines on ensuring full operational autonomy and an untainted, truly independent attribution mechanism were rejected, Sweden votes against this draft resolution.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The Russian draft resolution creates a politically compromised mechanism that subordinates investigative findings and methodology to the Security Council, effectively preserving Russia's veto over attribution. As all UK red lines regarding the mechanism's independence and reporting were rejected, the UK must vote against this draft resolution in accordance with its established policy.
reasons.United States of America: The Russian draft resolution creates a flawed, non-independent mechanism designed to shield the Syrian regime and subject investigative conclusions to a Russian veto, directly contradicting core U.S. red lines.

before.Bolivia (Plurinational State of):
Bolivia will vote in favour of the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation. We reiterate our absolute condemnation of the use of toxic chemicals as weapons under any circumstances, by anyone, anywhere. Such acts are unjustifiable and constitute serious crimes that must be thoroughly investigated so that those responsible can be held accountable.

To that end, it is vital that any investigative mechanism be truly independent, impartial, objective, transparent, and completely depoliticized. The establishment of the United Nations Independent Mechanism of Investigation, operating on the basis of rigorous on-site investigations, strict respect for the chain of custody of evidence, and full adherence to the Chemical Weapons Convention and the Charter of the United Nations, provides a necessary and credible instrument. We also firmly reject any attempts to use unverified allegations as a pretext for unilateral military actions that would violate the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and further aggravate the conflict.
before.France:
France will vote against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. 

Following the horrific chemical attack perpetrated in Douma on 7 April, which shocked the conscience of the world, our collective duty is to establish the truth, identify the perpetrators, and ensure that those responsible are held accountable. Yet the draft resolution before us does not aim to establish a truly independent, impartial, and effective attribution mechanism. On the contrary, it seeks to create a mechanism whose hands would be tied from the outset, whose investigative methodology would be strictly constrained, and whose findings would ultimately be subject to a political filter and a right of veto in this Council. 

We cannot accept a text that seeks to discredit established OPCW standards, imposes impossible preconditions on investigators, and offers the Syrian regime and its allies political control over conclusions regarding chemical weapons use. We need a truly independent mechanism, modeled on the Joint Investigative Mechanism that Russia previously dismantled with its vetoes, not an instrument designed to protect perpetrators from accountability. For these reasons, France will vote against this text.
before.Netherlands:
The Kingdom of the Netherlands will vote against the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation. 

First and foremost, accountability for the use of chemical weapons is essential, and any investigative mechanism must be genuinely independent, impartial, and professional. The mechanism proposed in this draft resolution does not meet these fundamental standards. Instead, it seeks to impose unwarranted operational constraints on investigators, micromanaging their methodology and evidence-gathering, while subjecting their findings on attribution to political filtering by the Security Council rather than respecting independent, expert conclusions. 

We cannot accept a text that undermines the established standards and autonomy of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons or creates an investigation tailored to shield perpetrators. For these reasons, the Netherlands will vote against this draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation:
Today, the Security Council has an opportunity to take a genuinely constructive, depoliticized, and professional step to address allegations of the use of chemical weapons in Syria. The draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation establishes a truly impartial, independent, and professional investigative mechanism — the United Nations Independent Mechanism of Investigation (UNIMI) — to identify those responsible for the use of toxic chemicals as weapons. 

Unlike flawed predecessors that relied on remote assessments and third-party materials of dubious origin, our draft establishes clear, objective standards strictly in accordance with the Chemical Weapons Convention, insisting on mandatory on-site visits, a rigorous and verifiable chain of custody for all physical and biomedical samples, and recruitment based on broad and balanced geographical representation. Crucially, it respects the Charter of the United Nations by preserving the Security Council's primary prerogative to consider the mechanism's findings and determine appropriate measures.

Furthermore, following the formal invitation extended by the Syrian Government to the Technical Secretariat of the OPCW to send a Fact-Finding Mission directly to Douma, our text welcomes that deployment and calls upon all parties to provide full cooperation and security. There is no legitimate reason to oppose this balanced and objective text, unless the goal of certain Western delegations is not to establish the truth through professional investigation, but rather to use fabricated pretexts to justify unlawful military aggression against a sovereign State. We urge all members of the Security Council to vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom will vote against this draft resolution. 

Let us be completely clear about what is happening today. Following the horrific chemical weapons attack in Douma on Saturday, which shocked the conscience of the world, we need an independent, impartial, and highly professional mechanism to attribute responsibility for chemical weapons attacks in Syria. That is precisely what the Council had in the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism, until Russia used its veto repeatedly to kill it when its findings proved uncomfortable for the Syrian regime.

The draft resolution before us today does not establish an independent mechanism. Instead, it creates a mechanism in name only—one designed to shield the Syrian authorities from accountability. Under this proposal, the mechanism’s terms of reference, its methodology, and ultimately its findings would be subject to political filtering and a Russian veto in this Council. A mechanism whose conclusions can simply be blocked by the perpetrator's protector is not an investigative body; it is a sham. 

Because Russia has refused to address these fundamental flaws and continues to prioritize protecting the Syrian regime over upholding the global taboo against the use of chemical weapons, the United Kingdom cannot and will not support this text.
before.United States of America:
The United States will vote against this resolution. 

Let us be completely clear about what this Russian text is and what it is not. It is not an impartial mechanism to hold perpetrators of chemical weapons attacks accountable. Rather, it is a transparent attempt to shield the Assad regime from accountability and provide Russia with a veto over any findings that point to Damascus. 

Russia killed the Joint Investigative Mechanism last fall because it dared to confirm what the world already knew: that the Syrian regime uses chemical weapons against its own people. Now, after the horrors we saw unfold in Douma just days ago, Russia puts forward a text designed to ensure that no truly independent, credible, and objective investigation can ever take place. This draft resolution imposes unacceptable preconditions on investigators, ties their hands on methodology, and ensures that the Security Council—where Russia holds a veto—would cherry-pick the findings and decide whether perpetrators are ever named. 

We cannot accept a sham mechanism designed to guarantee impunity. For these reasons, the United States will vote "no."

after.China:
China’s position on the issue of chemical weapons has been consistent and clear. We are firmly opposed to the use of chemical weapons by any State, organization or individual, anywhere, under any circumstances and for any purpose. Anyone who uses chemical weapons must be held accountable.

China is deeply concerned by the recent allegations regarding the use of chemical weapons in Syria. We support a comprehensive, objective and impartial investigation into the incident, based on solid facts and science, so as to arrive at a conclusion that can stand the test of time and history. 

Proceeding from that position of principle, China voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. The draft resolution clearly condemned the use of toxic chemicals as weapons, supported the prompt deployment of the Fact-Finding Mission of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons to Douma to conduct an on-site investigation, and proposed the establishment of a United Nations Independent Mechanism of Investigation that would operate on the basis of high professional standards, strict adherence to the Chemical Weapons Convention, the preservation of the chain of custody, and direct on-site visits. These elements are constructive and fully in line with our objective of establishing the facts through depoliticized and professional means. We regret that the Council was unable to adopt the draft resolution.

China has always maintained that the Security Council must maintain unity on the issue of chemical weapons in Syria. Dialogue and consultation are the only viable path to bridging differences. Prejudging the outcome of investigations or taking unilateral action outside the framework of the Security Council will only further complicate the situation and undermine the political process. 

China calls upon all parties concerned to remain calm and exercise restraint, avoid any escalation of tensions, and support the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission in carrying out an objective and impartial investigation. At the same time, the international community should remain committed to the political settlement of the Syrian issue under the framework of resolution 2254 (2015), respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, and continue to support the United Nations as the main channel of mediation. China stands ready to continue to play a positive and constructive role to that end.
after.Kuwait:
Kuwait abstained in the voting on the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation, and I should like to explain the reasons for our vote.

Kuwait’s position on the issue of chemical weapons is principled, firm, and well known. We condemn in the strongest possible terms the use of chemical weapons by any party, anywhere, and under any circumstances. Such heinous acts constitute a flagrant violation of international law, international humanitarian law, and relevant Security Council resolutions, particularly resolution 2118 (2013). Those responsible for the use of these horrific weapons must be held accountable and brought to justice, and there can be no impunity for such crimes.

Following the tragic and alarming reports of the use of toxic chemicals in Douma on 7 April, which resulted in the loss of dozens of innocent civilian lives, including women and children, our priority has been to ensure the establishment of an independent, impartial, objective, and professional mechanism to investigate these allegations and identify those responsible. 

Earlier today, Kuwait voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the United States because we believed it established a credible and independent mechanism capable of carrying out attribution without political interference. 

With regard to the draft resolution just voted on, Kuwait decided to abstain because the text does not command the necessary consensus among Council members, and because we have serious reservations regarding the modalities of the proposed mechanism, particularly the provisions that subject the mechanism’s findings to a political filter by the Security Council, thereby undermining its independence and impartiality. 

Kuwait deeply regrets that the Security Council remains divided on such a critical issue affecting international peace and security and the lives of innocent Syrian civilians. We reiterate our full support for the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons and welcome the deployment of its Fact-Finding Mission to Douma. We call upon all parties to provide full, immediate, and safe access so that the Mission can carry out its mandate without delay or obstruction.
after.Russian Federation:
The outcome of the vote on the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation is extremely revealing. It has laid bare the real intentions and priorities of our Western colleagues. 

Today, the Council was presented with a genuine, balanced, and constructive opportunity to establish a truly independent, impartial, and highly professional mechanism to investigate allegations of chemical weapons use and identify perpetrators. Our draft resolution was based strictly on the norms of international law, the provisions of the Chemical Weapons Convention, and the highest standards of evidence, including mandatory on-site visits and an untainted chain of custody. 

Yet the United States, the United Kingdom, France, and their allies chose to vote against it. By doing so, they have shown the entire world that they do not need the truth. They do not need an objective and depoliticized investigation. What they wanted was not an impartial investigative body, but a convenient geopolitical tool—a compliant instrument that would rubber-stamp predetermined accusations against Damascus, entirely devoid of direct evidence and reliant on fabricated social media videos produced by terrorist-linked organizations like the White Helmets. 

Our Western partners are simply terrified of a real, on-site, professional investigation because it would inevitably dismantle the slanderous campaign they have orchestrated. They have already assigned guilt, issued ultimatums, and are now openly threatening the illegal use of military force against a sovereign Member State of the United Nations, in flagrant violation of the United Nations Charter. 

We thank those delegations that supported our draft resolution and demonstrated a responsible approach to maintaining international peace and security. As for those who voted against it, the responsibility for undermining efforts to establish accountability and for any dangerous escalation that may follow rests entirely on their shoulders.
after.Sweden:
Sweden voted against the draft resolution just put to the vote.

The horrifying reports and images of the chemical weapons attack in Douma on 7 April have shocked us all. The use of chemical weapons is an unacceptable violation of international law, a war crime, and a threat to international peace and security. Those responsible must be identified and held accountable. There can be no impunity for such heinous acts.

To achieve this, we need a mechanism that is genuinely independent, impartial, objective, and professional, building on the established work and standards of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) and the former Joint Investigative Mechanism. 

Unfortunately, the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation does not meet these essential criteria. Rather than establishing a truly independent attribution mechanism, it seeks to unduly restrict the methodology and independence of the investigators and subjects their findings to political filtering and decision-making within the Security Council. We cannot support a mechanism whose independence is compromised from the outset and whose findings would be subject to political considerations rather than scientific and expert evaluation. That is why we voted against it.

At the same time, Sweden fully supports the immediate deployment of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission to Douma to establish the facts on the ground. We call on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to grant the Fact-Finding Mission full, safe, and unfettered access to all sites, witnesses, and materials without any delay or hindrance.

The victims of Douma and all victims of chemical weapons attacks in Syria deserve justice and accountability. The Council must remain united in upholding the international norm against chemical weapons.
